# Instructions for GitHub Copilot code review on Aivera

Aivera ranks job candidates on evidence of their work and holds their CVs and assessments (UAE and KSA). The full rulebook is [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md); review every pull request against it and against the Gherkin acceptance criteria of the ticket named in the PR body.

## Review for these first (any miss is a blocker)

- **Workspace isolation, two layers:** every workspace-owned table has `workspace_id`, a row-level security policy on `nullif(current_setting('app.workspace_id', true), '')::uuid`, `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, and repository queries that also filter by workspace inside `withWorkspace` (ADR-005). Flag any query outside `withWorkspace`, any client-supplied workspace id, any RLS bypass.
- **Server-side authorisation** on every server action, route handler and worker job (workspace, role, job). Hiding UI is never the control.
- **Candidate personal data** (names, contacts, CV text, evidence, scores, interview notes) never in logs, telemetry, URLs, query strings, error text or browser storage.
- **A person makes every hiring decision:** nothing rejects, advances, contacts or shares a candidate without a previewed, confirmed action; decisions are audited.
- **Scores cite evidence;** an unsupported claim counts zero; metrics state observed / baseline / projection / not yet available.
- **Paying never changes ranking:** assessment, jobs and intake never import billing or portfolio.
- **Migrations** generated by Drizzle Kit, forward-only, never an edit to a committed migration; no cross-schema foreign keys.
- **Secrets** never committed; synthetic data only (`docs/00-product/personas.md`).

## Then review for Ponytail discipline (the smallest complete change)

Every PR must be the smallest change that fully solves its ticket. Flag:

- Code nobody asked for: speculative options, config, abstractions, wrappers, "for later" code, unused exports.
- Reinvented helpers when the codebase, the standard library, the platform or an installed dependency already does it.
- A new dependency without a reason in the PR body (what it replaces, why not the platform).
- New logic (branch, parser, score, money, security, tenancy) without a test, or a safety test without a `// SAFETY: mutation check:` comment.
- A known limit without a `shortcut: <limit>, <when to upgrade>` comment.
- A weakened lint rule, test, threshold or CI step.

## Architecture and front end

- Modules are imported only as `@aivera/<m>` (contracts); `/composition` only from apps (ADR-002).
- Front-end features keep the layers `domain/ services/ hooks/ components/` (ADR-003); components are presentational `.tsx`; no cross-feature imports of hooks, services or components.
- A screen is built from its artboard file in `docs/01-design/artboards/` (map: `docs/01-design/screens.md`). Flag any section, element, panel, logo, copy, type size or control height the artboard draws that the change leaves out without a listed reason.
- UI uses `@aivera/ui` and Case file tokens only: no hex colours, no arbitrary Tailwind values where a token exists, no hard-coded user-facing strings; WCAG 2.2 AA; one primary button per view; the highlighter only on cited evidence, except the website, candidate home and sign-in page places DESIGN.md names.

## How to comment

Be specific: file and line, what is wrong in one sentence, and the fix. Group as Blocker / Should fix / Nit. Do not comment on formatting (Prettier and oxlint run in CI).
